historicalObligations.title: Durable worklog queue acceptance must not claim email delivery
Notification actor isolation and actual change approval
Credential boundaries, reload, resumability and independent checks
Preserve flat task lifecycle responses and uncertain-outcome reconciliation
Preserve query aliases, filtered counts and paging in all four ticket lists
Preserve named task priorities and atomic invalid-edit rejection
Preserve governed change state, approval, edit-lock and lifecycle routes
Preserve customer authentication routes, provider authority and delivery evidence
Preserve executable schemas, previews and autonomous AI report binding
Reject unsupported ticket edit fields atomically
Preserve four fixed raw reads without arbitrary raw access
Preserve mail dialog cancellation, reasons, evidence and queue behavior
Preserve authority, transport, identifier and prerequisite contracts
Profile summary latency against a prospectively agreed budget while preserving correct counts
Verify the actual configured HTTP execution identity and access

scenarios.title: Explicit owner delegation and live revocation boundaries
Owned incident, request, change and task lifecycles
Owner creation and tenant/customer self-service automation
Genuine paired automation with immutable attempt history
Actual AI provider dispatch, reports, logs and bound event identity
Captured delivery lifecycle and safe reviewed retries
Support setup, actual recipients and actor-isolated decisions
Tenant, account, role and branding administration
Exact effort and readable historical worklogs
Closed schemas, bounded behavior and independent transport checks

limitations: This contract is an evidence format and test plan, not evidence of a live campaign.
The validator verifies identity bindings, checksums, complete denominators, recorded observations and assertions; it cannot establish that supplied captures are authentic.
One authentication-mode lane does not establish all-authentication-modes production acceptance.
Historic named-owner and human-signature fields remain in the original register; this technical campaign neither invents nor requires those signatures.
